_doc: OSCAR Figure 4 (RIGHT), Qwen3-8B column: job-level throughput at a fixed 100k
input as a function of batch size, with prefix warm-up.
Paper OSCAR speedup vs BF16: 2.88 / 3.35 / 3.44 at BS=1 / 8 / 32.
Paper Saw-INT4: 1.52 / 2.32 / 2.09 -- not implemented here, series absent.
The shared prefix is what makes BS=32 at 100k feasible: 32 x 100k = 3.2M
tokens exceeds the pool, but one shared prefix costs ~100k plus short tails.
Paper Fig 4 right for this model -- OSCAR speedup vs BF16: 3.08 / 5.19 / 6.17 at BS=1 / 8 / 32.

Uses SGLANG_MIXED_KV_PREFIX_REUSE_ACROSS_CHUNKS on the quant arms instead of --chunked-prefill-size 102400. The flag fixes the actual defect (a per-chunk positional bound min-accumulated with ownership-backed bounds, latching prefix reuse at chunk 1); the chunk override merely sidestepped it by making the prompt fit one chunk, which disabled chunked prefill, OOM'd bf16, and forced mem-frac to 0.82. bf16 does not need the flag -- it already caches across chunks.

vq2 arm uses the Qwen3-8B codebook. Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 has IDENTICAL KV geometry (36 layers, 8 kv-heads, head_dim 128), so it loads unchanged and the decode kernel does exactly the same work -- the gather, dequant and dot are independent of codebook CONTENTS. THROUGHPUT ONLY: the centroids encode the wrong model's statistics, so any accuracy number from this arm is meaningless and must not be reported.

WORKLOAD = replay: BS DISTINCT 100k prompts, the set run twice with the second measured, so each request hits its OWN cached KV ('immediate replay after warmup', the protocol named in the paper's Fig 6 caption). This makes KV capacity bind -- 32x100k = 3.2M tokens against a ~374k bf16 pool vs ~2.4M for int2 -- which is the effect the batch panel is measuring. The shared-prefix variant stores the context once for everyone and therefore erases it.

BS=2/4 fill the transition. bf16 holds ~3.3 x 100k prompts (334k-374k pool at 144 KB/token); OSCAR holds ~21 (2.1-2.4M at ~18 KB/token). So BS=4 is exactly bf16's cliff: 3 resident, 1 queued, while OSCAR absorbs all four. Between BS=1 (both fit, 2.68x) and BS=8 (bf16 thrashing, 6.09x).
